startup.name: Text.ai
startup.one_liner: Alfi, your group chat with social skills to bring friends closer
startup.description: Consumer AI assistant that lives in a friend group chat, remembers preferences, books restaurants, makes group images, tracks a social calendar and summarises the chat. Revenue model is not stated. Team of 4 in San Francisco, Spring 2025 batch.

yc_acceptance.basis: The company is listed in the Spring 2025 batch, so acceptance is already known; this reports the prior for completeness. Starting rate is about 1 percent with a 0.6 to 2 percent band (yc_acceptance.md). Up to 3 percent for a team of 4 building a live AI product in a hot area, held there because consumer social without repeat usage is penalised and no traction is stated.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly decline because consumer group chat apps depend on every member adopting at once, the pitch gives no retention or usage number, and the largest messaging platforms can add an AI participant in weeks. A founder story about Gen Z leaving broadcast social is a thesis, not evidence of a paying or compounding habit.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry Consumer --years 2022-2026 --calibration-only: seed 32% / 43% / 57% (lower / known only / upper), cond 43% (n=21); Series A 0% / 0% / 25%, cond 0% (n=9). Wider cohort: Consumer all years known seed 77% overall.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Set at 0.93 times the 43 percent consumer anchor: a four person team, a consumer social wedge and no stated traction give no reason to lift it, and the winners test shows lifts for hot sectors did not separate raisers from non-raisers. Forecast window: 19 months, from 2025-04-07 to 2026-11-17. Seed means a financing round above about $1M from outside investors that closes inside the window; the YC deal does not count. Calibrated on knowledge/tables/time_to_milestones.csv (Consumer median 5.5 months to seed, p75 19.0) about 90 percent of eventual seeds land in this window. These odds do not rank this company against others.

bands.rationale: Small post YC round under $3M from angels and a pre-seed fund, the commonest result for a thin team. The 2022 and later seed 25th percentile of $2.8M in knowledge/tables/round_benchmarks.csv sits at its top edge. The standard $500K YC deal is excluded because the window counts only rounds above $1M.
Institutional seed near the 2022 and later median of $4.1M, in line with the 3.0M deal size in the current NVCA data cited in stage_benchmarks.md.
A larger institutional seed, which the 2022 and later 75th percentile of $6.5M and press reported 2026 raises (median $6.0M) make plausible but not typical.
Upside seed of a hot category lead investor; rare for a small team.

ladder.why_it_fails: A four person consumer social product has to show that groups keep using an AI participant, and that evidence is hard to produce in 19 months. Investors have funded few consumer social apps since the Guilded and Squad exits, which both needed years and a gaming or video niche. Alfi also asks every member of a group to switch apps or add a bot, so growth is capped by the slowest friend. Most likely the company ends the window with the YC deal, a few thousand users and no lead.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --industry Consumer --years 2022-2026 --calibration-only: Series A cond 0% (n=9); overall calibration conditional A given seed 45% (n=279); B2B 2022+ cond 23% (n=84).
anchors.adjustment_reason: Window limited: median months to Series A is 28 (calibration sample) so few companies reach A before month 19, and the conditional rate here counts only A rounds closing inside the same window. Reaching a Series A years later is common for companies with paying customers, so this is not the ever number.

bands.rationale: Thin Series A or extended seed labelled A, below the 2022 and later 25th percentile of $10M.
Central band around the 2022 and later median of $14.2M.
Strong growth round near the 75th percentile of $20M and above.
Breakout lead round for a category leader with fast growth, rare in any cohort of the data.

ladder.why_it_fails: Consumer companies rarely reach Series A in the window: the Consumer 2022 and later cohort shows 0 of 9 seed companies reaching A so far. A round needs retained group usage, a revenue model beyond restaurant referrals and an answer to Apple, Meta and OpenAI shipping group AI features, and nothing in the pitch shows these yet.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only: Series B given Series A 44 percent known only (n=126), lower and upper bounds 8 and 53 percent unconditional. This is an ever number, not inside the window.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Set about 0.7 times the 44 percent conditional rate because newer batches show only 16 to 23 percent in B2B 2022 and later cohorts so far (right censored). It is an ever figure and is not in the window.

bands.rationale: Down or flat round below the 2022 and later 25th percentile of $25M.
Central band around the 2022 and later median of $37M.
Strong round near the 75th percentile of $57M.
Breakout growth round for a category leader, seen in only a few percent of Series B rounds in the data.

ladder.why_it_fails: Most companies that raise a Series A do not raise a Series B because growth slows against the A plan, burn rises faster than revenue, or the category consolidates around two leaders. Investors at B want repeatable sales or usage economics, and a company that grew on a founder-led motion often cannot show them. Analogs such as the acquired or stalled A stage companies in the cohort show that about half stop here.

anchors.source: python3 -I scripts/base_rates.py --calibration-only: Series C given Series B 36 percent known only (n=55); Series D or later given C 40 percent (n=20). Ever number.
anchors.adjustment_reason: Held at 0.75 times the 36 percent anchor because the cohort is small and late stage data is incomplete; counted ever, years outside the window.

bands.rationale: Thin or down round; Series C medians fell from $64M to $45M between 2018 to 2021 and 2022 and later (n=6 and 9).
Central band near the 2022 and later median of $45M.
Strong growth round for a company that has kept compounding, above the 2022 and later median.
Category leader round, rare and mostly seen for companies that won their market outright.

ladder.why_it_fails: At Series C the bar is a clear path to a very large outcome, so companies fail here when growth decelerates below what a late stage fund underwrites, when a platform owner or a better funded rival wins the category, or when the market stays smaller than the pitch. Only 6 percent of the calibration sample reached C at the known only count, and the survivors mostly had hard to copy distribution or technology.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Consumer social companies in YC history mostly end as small acquihires or fade: Squad was bought by Twitter and shut the next day, Glimpse was folded into another tool, and Rume and Assorted Bits are inactive. Reaching a meaningful exit needs a habit loop that spreads inside groups, and the incumbent messengers hold the distribution.

analogs.relevance: Group video app for friends and communities, Winter 2018.
analogs.outcome_summary: Raised a $5M seed in 2019 led by First Round and was acquired by Twitter in 2020 with the app shut the next day: a soft landing, not a scale outcome.
Series A of $7M in 2020, sold to Roblox in 2021 for about $77.6M; won a niche (gaming) on features Discord lacked, which is the path a group chat product needs.
Pivoted from friend video chats to group matching, acquired in 2022 by Twine with no post YC round found; incumbent copying noted.

analogs.relevance: Three person social video chat, Summer 2020.
analogs.outcome_summary: Raised a small seed and closed after about two years; no cause found, and Zoom and other chat tools were crowded rivals.

analogs.relevance: Mobile social calendar for hangouts with friends, Summer 2012.
analogs.outcome_summary: Inactive; the same social calendar idea Alfi lists, with no public post mortem.

killers.risk: Group adoption: every friend must join or add the bot, so growth stalls below the size where the product is useful.
killers.evidence: An analysis of AI group chat products argues that the hard part is getting all of a user's friends to switch, per spyglass.org group chat piece; a four person team has no distribution channel stated.
killers.mitigation: Start inside existing group chats via a bot or SMS and seed one dense community such as a campus.

killers.risk: Platform copy: Apple Messages, WhatsApp, Instagram or ChatGPT add group AI features with built in distribution.
killers.evidence: OpenAI already runs a chat app approaching a billion users and Meta owns the main group messengers, so a feature clone needs only months.
killers.mitigation: Pick a vertical group job such as trip planning where a general assistant is weak.

killers.risk: No revenue model: restaurant booking referrals and image generation do not yield a venture sized business, so investors see a feature, not a company.
killers.evidence: The description lists features but no pricing or revenue; Squad needed a First Round seed and still ended as an acquihire.
killers.mitigation: Test a paid tier for group memory and planning, and show cohort retention at week 8.

technical_complexity.rationale: Chat, LLM calls, Yelp booking and image generation are all assembled from existing APIs, so a small team can ship in weeks. The hard parts are per group memory, reading social context without being annoying, and distribution on closed messaging platforms, which is a product and growth problem more than an engineering one.

takeover_risk.rationale: Any large messenger can add a group AI participant with its own model access and billions of users, and the use cases listed (booking, image generation, summaries) are general features rather than a moat. The standalone app also depends on platform rules for bots in third party chats.

evidence.claim: AI chat products are heading to group settings, with several startups launching in 2025, showing interest but not paid demand.
Conversational commerce is projected to grow from about $11B in 2025, a broad figure not specific to group chat.

roadmap.goal: Show that one group uses Alfi weekly without prompting.
actions: Launch in 20 real friend groups and record weekly active groups and messages the bot starts.
Interview group planners about what they pay with time today.
roadmap.proof: At least 10 groups still active after 8 weeks.

roadmap.goal: Retention and a first revenue signal that investors can compare to other consumer apps.
actions: Run a paid tier test for memory and planning.
Publish week 8 group retention and invites per group.
roadmap.proof: Group retention above 30 percent at week 8 and a measured paid conversion.

roadmap.goal: A repeatable growth loop with margins that survive model costs.
actions: Make the invite loop product led so each active group brings another.
Cut inference cost per active group below revenue per group.
roadmap.proof: Organic growth above 10 percent per month and positive gross margin.

weaknesses: Generic and hard to search, with a .ai domain suffix that reads as a tool
The product character is called Alfi, so the company name and product name differ
brand.rationale: The company name describes a category and is hard to own, unlike past consumer brands such as Discord or Guilded that were distinctive. The mascot name Alfi is friendlier and would be the better brand, but the split adds confusion for a consumer growth product.

narrative.headline: A cheap, plausible consumer AI product with no stated traction and weak group adoption economics: seed odds near the consumer anchor.
narrative.general_summary: Text.ai builds Alfi, an AI participant for friend group chats that plans meals, calendars and images. The idea is easy to build and sits where Gen Z behaviour is moving, but consumer social products have a poor record in YC data: Squad, Guilded and Glimpse ended in acquisitions, mostly soft landings, and Rume and Assorted Bits closed. The Consumer 2022 and later cohort reached seed at 43 percent known only and none reached Series A so far. A 19 month window gives a seed probability of 0.40, close to the anchor, because the winners test showed hot sector lifts do not separate raisers. Series A inside the window is unlikely.

assumptions: Description only; no traction or revenue was given.
Window is 19 months; probabilities for seed and Series A are inside it, while Series B and C are ever figures.
Comps reflect older cohorts; the web search for market context returned a page naming this company which was ignored (LEAK-WEB: text-ai).
